lc_person: Pearl Kibre, medieval historian at Hunter College; author of Hippocrates Latinus and The Library of Pico della Mirandola.
item_person: Pearl Kibre, historian at Hunter College, educated at Columbia University; LC identifier n85174095 and BnF identifier 120539340.

evidence.says: LC heads the authority Kibre, Pearl, 1903-. Its source notes identify the author of Hippocrates Latinus (1985), a medieval historian who studied at Berkeley and Columbia and taught mainly at Hunter College. The biographical-dictionary note explicitly gives birth year 1903 and death year 1985.

Pearl Kibre is a historian with Hunter College as employer and Columbia University among her educational institutions. The item gives birth year 1900, death year 1985, P244 n85174095, BnF 120539340, VIAF 61565443 and ISNI 0000000110278880. Its birth statement has no reference.

BnF identifies Kibre, Pearl (1900-1985), explicitly gives birth year 1900 and death year 1985, and describes a historian with a Columbia doctorate. Its sources include both Hippocrates latinus (1985) and The library of Pico della Mirandola (1936); ISNI 0000000110278880 matches Wikidata.

The University of Pennsylvania archival finding aid identifies Pearl Kibre (1900-1985), a historian of medieval history and science who received her Columbia PhD in 1936 and taught at Hunter College and the City University Graduate Center. Its creator heading retains the older 1903- authority form.

The catalogue record attributes The library of Pico della Mirandola to Pearl Kibre, published by Columbia University Press in 1936, with the edition note Thesis (Ph. D.)--Columbia university, 1936. This matches the graph’s AHA dissertation title, institution and year.

notes: The birth discrepancy concerns one historian: matching affiliation, identifiers and works establish identity. Prefer 1900 on the agreement of BnF and the university archival biography, while retaining the documented conflict with LC’s 1903. LC’s biographical note also gives a 1937 doctorate; the dissertation catalogue and Penn biography support the graph’s 1936.
